sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: Distinguish a chemical DNA mark from a changed base sequence, and see why location and cell context change its interpretation.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The mark→context→hypothesis→test Mermaid is a good inference boundary but never shows the molecular distinction behind the bookmarks analogy: the same base letters with a chemical mark versus different sequence letters. That is the newcomer bottleneck.
accuracyGuardrails: Keep DNA methylation distinct from histone marks, 5mC from5hmC and position-dependent regulation from universal silencing; do not depict a mark as proving a treatment response.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: Aligned AACGT rows isolate the chemical C mark from an actual C-to-T substitution. DNA and histone substrates are labeled separately;5mC versus5hmC limitation and promoter/gene-body location prompt remain explicit. Both original answered reasoning and added sequence/mark retrieval check resist universal silencing, cell-fraction and treatment inference.
